notes: Two independent review passes reached the same substantive error conclusion. The earliest incorrect process item is S3.2, which states that an accepted start leaves parity and done unchanged. The one-cycle done semantics require done to clear on the cycle following an accepted finish, including when that following cycle simultaneously accepts a new start. The RTL correctly defaults done to zero before evaluating the start/finish/bit branches, so a start immediately after a finish clears the previous done pulse rather than preserving it. In the second review, the concrete finish-at-N followed by accepted-start-at-N+1 sequence independently reproduced the contradiction. S3.5 contains a later related overstatement that all other cycles hold registers, because an otherwise ignored cycle may still clear the previous one-cycle done pulse. The final RTL itself correctly implements start, accumulation, final-bit inclusion, result hold, gating, and one-cycle done behavior, and trusted directed simulation and bounded formal verification pass all configured obligations.
